question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a regular disposable syringe?

options.A: It locks automatically after one use to prevent reuse
options.B: It doesn't need a needle to deliver medication
options.C: It can be easily washed and sterilized for another patient
options.D: It is made entirely of recycled plastic

explanation: Exactly right! Auto-disable syringes have a clever built-in stop that keeps the plunger from pulling back a second time, keeping everyone safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h2)

question: Where should you drop a used needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.A: Inside a puncture-resistant safety box
options.B: Back inside its original plastic wrapper
options.C: In the general office waste basket
options.D: On top of the treatment trolley tray

explanation: Well done! Always drop used sharps straight into a safety box to prevent accidental needle pricks on the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h2)

question: In ward inventory, what does hitting your 'minimum stock level' tell you?

options.A: It is the exact number of items used in a single day
options.B: It is the warning sign that tells you to place a new order
options.C: It is the maximum amount the store can hold
options.D: It shows the total financial budget for the clinic

explanation: That's correct! Think of minimum stock as your alarm bell—when supplies drop to this point, it's time to reorder so you don't run out. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h3)

question: How should a nurse manager figure out how many safety boxes to order for next month?

options.A: By doubling the number of expired items thrown away last year
options.B: By matching the exact number of doctors on duty
options.C: Based on past patient use and expected service volume
options.D: By guessing a random number that fits on the form

explanation: Spot on! Smart ordering looks at past consumption trends and expected patient numbers so you don't overstock or run short. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you must do before filling out a supply requisition form?

options.A: Travel directly to the central medical warehouse
options.B: Throw all remaining safety boxes in the incinerator
options.C: Write a complaint letter to the hospital director
options.D: Count the physical stock currently on your ward shelves

explanation: You got it! You always need to see what is physically on hand before you can figure out what is missing. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why does a requisition form need a supervisor's review and signature before heading to the store?

options.A: To stop nurses from talking to warehouse workers
options.B: To delay delivery and keep storerooms empty
options.C: To give the medical director extra paperwork to sign
options.D: To confirm that what you asked for matches your actual usage

explanation: Exactly! Authorization checks help catch mistakes, prevent over-ordering, and keep everything transparent. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h4)

question: What is the main job of a bin card attached to a storage shelf?

options.A: To give instructions on treating needle stick injuries
options.B: To advertise the brand name of the syringe maker
options.C: To show a running balance of stock movements in real time
options.D: To list phone numbers of delivery drivers

explanation: Well done! A bin card acts as a quick ledger right at the shelf, tracking every item added or taken away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is a big benefit of using digital inventory systems instead of paper records?

options.A: It ensures clinical injections never cause skin pain
options.B: It completely stops nurses from ever needing to count items
options.C: It lets central managers view stock data across sites quickly
options.D: It stops medical supplies from reaching their expiration date

explanation: Spot on! Digital systems link different clinics together, making it super easy to spot trends and shortages early. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: In medical storage, what does the FEFO rule stand for?

options.A: First-Expired, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Entry, Fast-Output
options.C: Forward-Examination, Final-Order
options.D: First-Evaluated, Freight-Out

explanation: You nailed it! FEFO means items closest to their expiry date get used first so nothing goes to waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is it important to keep cardboard safety boxes away from damp floors?

options.A: Moisture helps safety boxes assemble themselves
options.B: Water makes the needles inside sharper and safer
options.C: Wet cardboard attracts helpful insects to the room
options.D: Dampness weakens the cardboard and causes dangerous leaks

explanation: That's right! Water ruins cardboard rigidity, which can lead to nasty punctures or fluid leaks from used sharps. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the best immediate step for a clinic facing a sudden stockout of syringes?

options.A: Tell nursing staff to wash and reuse standard syringes
options.B: Borrow supplies from a nearby cooperating facility
options.C: Stop providing all injection treatments indefinitely
options.D: Wait patiently for the next quarterly delivery

explanation: Brilliant! Emergency borrowing between friendly neighboring clinics bridges the gap safely without resorting to dangerous reuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to reduce waste in a hospital store?

options.A: Checking inventory expiration dates every month
options.B: Keeping storage rooms dry, clean, and out of direct sunlight
options.C: Rotating stock properly using FEFO
options.D: Ordering huge quantities far beyond what past data suggests

explanation: You got it! Over-ordering leads straight to expired stock and wasted money—definitely a practice to avoid! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary danger of running out of injection safety commodities at a health clinic?

options.A: Clinicians may resort to reusing single-use equipment.
options.B: Medications will automatically expire much faster.
options.C: The cost of electricity at the facility will increase.
options.D: Patients will completely stop visiting the facility for care.

explanation: When basic injection supplies run out, desperate staff may unfortunately reuse disposable syringes, spreading infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is accurate quantification of injection commodities important for a healthcare facility?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for medical waste disposal.
options.B: It reduces the total number of nursing staff needed on duty.
options.C: It guarantees that every patient will receive an antibiotic.
options.D: It prevents dangerous stockouts and costly item expiration.

explanation: Good estimation ensures enough supplies are available to prevent shortages while avoiding excess stock that expires on the shelf. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a conventional disposable syringe?

options.A: It can be washed and sterilized multiple times safely.
options.B: It locks or breaks automatically to prevent second use.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of liquid than any other type.
options.D: It is made entirely of soft, flexible rubber material.

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a built-in mechanism that renders them completely unusable after one single stroke. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a safety box in a clinical injection setting?

options.A: To measure precise doses of liquid drugs for patients
options.B: To store brand-new, sterile syringes away from dust and moisture
options.C: To transport mixed liquid medications safely to the bedside
options.D: To safely collect used needles and syringes before disposal

explanation: Safety boxes are puncture-resistant containers built specifically to hold used sharp items and protect staff from accidental needle sticks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why is a waste factor or buffer stock added when calculating injection commodities?

options.A: To provide extra income for the hospital pharmacy department
options.B: To ensure the facility has extra funds to pay staff salaries
options.C: To cover dropped items, training breakage, and accidental contamination
options.D: To account for patients who refuse to take their medications

explanation: A buffer percentage ensures unexpected item loss on the ward does not lead to a sudden shortage of clinical tools. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: A clinic notices a sudden influx of new patients moving into the local community. How should this affect their commodity calculations?

options.A: The safety box requirements should be completely ignored.
options.B: The clinic should switch exclusively to glass syringes.
options.C: The waste factor percentage must be reduced to zero.
options.D: The projected target population must be increased.

explanation: An increasing population means more people will need injections, requiring an upward adjustment in commodity estimation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: An immunization campaign targets 500 children, and each child requires 3 doses. Using a 10% waste factor, how many total syringes are needed?
explanation: First multiply 500 children by 3 doses to get 1,500 base items. Then multiply 1,500 by 1.10 (adding the 10% waste factor) to get 1,650. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: A local clinic plans to administer 4,000 curative injections over the next quarter without a waste factor. If each injection needs one syringe, how many syringes should be ordered?
explanation: Multiplying the total injection encounters by the dose per encounter without a waste factor gives the exact baseline total of 4,000. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: What must a nurse always do when a calculated safety box requirement results in a fractional number like 12.3 boxes?

options.A: Always round up to the next whole number.
options.B: Ignore the calculation and request an arbitrary box amount.
options.C: Discard the fraction and order only the exact whole integer.
options.D: Always round down to the nearest lower whole number.

explanation: Rounding up ensures you never run out of disposal containers for your used needles and syringes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: A clinic expects to use 2,000 syringes during a vaccination drive. If each safety box holds 100 syringes, how many safety boxes are required?
explanation: Divide the total number of used syringes (2,000) by the capacity of a single box (100), which equals 20 boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when estimating injection commodity needs?

options.A: Performing regular physical inventory audits on the ward
options.B: Ignoring existing stock levels currently sitting in the storeroom
options.C: Collaborating closely with pharmacy and supply chain personnel
options.D: Reviewing past consumption reports from previous months

explanation: Always subtract what is already in stock from your calculated requirement so you do not accidentally over-order. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why is it a major mistake to order powdered vaccines without ordering reconstitution syringes?

options.A: The powder cannot be safely mixed into a liquid solution for injection.
options.B: The nursing staff will be unable to document the doses on paper.
options.C: Patients will experience immediate allergic reactions to the dry powder.
options.D: The safety boxes will instantly melt when exposed to powdered medicine.

explanation: Powdered vaccines or medications must be diluted with a liquid using special mixing syringes before they can be drawn up and administered. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To record the daily vital signs and health status of admitted patients
options.B: To document the financial salaries and allowances of hospital workers
options.C: To schedule the duty shifts and off-days of the ward nursing staff
options.D: To track the exact quantity and movement of a specific supply item

explanation: A stock card functions as a ledger specifically designed to monitor inventory levels, showing when items enter and leave the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is inventory control considered a vital duty for ward nurses?

options.A: It prevents unexpected shortages of critical medical supplies during emergencies
options.B: It ensures that doctors write legible and accurate prescriptions daily
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for hospital management to buy new drugs
options.D: it stops patients from buying fake medications from outside pharmacies

explanation: Nurses manage ward stock so that life-saving items are always available when a patient suddenly deteriorates. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What does the balance column on a stock card represent?

options.A: The number of expired items thrown away that month
options.B: The maximum capacity the drug shelf can hold
options.C: The total amount of money spent on purchasing the item
options.D: The running total of remaining stock after each transaction

explanation: The balance updates continuously by adding receipts and subtracting issues to show what is currently available on the shelf. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: Why must a nurse sign or initial every entry made on a stock card?

options.A: To calculate the monthly salary bonus due to the nursing unit
options.B: To prevent the pharmacy department from reducing future supplies
options.C: To prove that the nurse worked extra hours on that specific day
options.D: To ensure accountability and provide a clear trail for audits

explanation: Signatures establish personal responsibility for every movement of stock, which is essential for investigating discrepancies later. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h2)

question: What triggers a nurse to place a new order for a medical supply item?

options.A: When the hospital accountant visits the ward for an inspection
options.B: When the stock balance drops down to the reorder level
options.C: When the expiration date of the current batch is reached
options.D: When the storage shelf is completely empty and bare

explanation: The reorder level acts as an early warning system, giving enough time for new supplies to arrive before safety stock is touched. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: A ward has a lead time of five days for syringes. What does this lead time actually mean?

options.A: It takes five days from placing the order until the syringes arrive on the ward
options.B: The ward will completely run out of all syringes in exactly five days
options.C: Syringes on the shelf will expire and spoil after five days of storage
options.D: Nurses must count the physical syringes every five days without fail

explanation: Lead time is the delivery window required for processing, packing, and transporting ordered goods to the requesting unit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to record items taken from the stock cupboard?

options.A: Immediately after the items are removed for use
options.B: Whenever the physical shelf looks empty or disorganized
options.C: Only when the central store manager asks for a report
options.D: At the end of every working week on Friday afternoon

explanation: Immediate recording prevents forgotten transactions and keeps the running balance accurate throughout the shift. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary danger of delaying stock card updates until the end of the week?

options.A: Hospital management will reduce the overall budget of the nursing unit
options.B: The central store will automatically double the next order quantity
options.C: Arithmetic errors and forgotten items lead to inaccurate stock balances
options.D: The medications on the shelf will automatically change their expiry dates

explanation: Relying on memory hours or days later results in guessing quantities, which destroys the reliability of the inventory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: How do seasonal disease trends influence how a nurse orders ward supplies?

options.A: They help nurses anticipate higher demand and order specific items ahead of time
options.B: They remove the need to calculate lead times when submitting requisitions
options.C: They dictate the exact time of day nurses must count the inventory
options.D: They change the physical maximum storage capacity of the drug cupboard

explanation: Anticipating disease patterns allows the ward to stock up on relevant treatments before an outbreak or seasonal surge hits. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: A ward nurse notices that the stock of intravenous cannula size 18 has fallen below the reorder level. What immediate action should be taken?

options.A: Prepare and submit a requisition form to replenish the stock
options.B: Hide the remaining cannulas in a drawer so nobody else uses them
options.C: Wait until the very last cannula is used before telling anyone
options.D: Borrow supplies from another ward without recording the transaction

explanation: Hitting the reorder level is the signal to order more supplies immediately before a stockout occurs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a necessary step when receiving new stock on the ward?

options.A: Verifying that the expiration dates on the products are acceptable
options.B: Checking the physical items against the quantities on the delivery note
options.C: Hiding the delivery notes so other staff members cannot read them
options.D: Inspecting the packaging for any signs of damage or leakage

explanation: Delivery notes are official records that should be kept accessible for audits, not hidden away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why is it important to check expiration dates immediately upon receiving new supplies?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of each individual item
options.B: To determine how many nursing staff members are needed on duty
options.C: To decide which shelf in the storage cupboard looks the cleanest
options.D: To prevent accepting short-dated stock that might expire before use

explanation: Catching expired or near-expiry goods upon delivery allows the facility to return them before accepting responsibility for wasted items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which Nigerian federal body is primarily responsible for setting national environmental protection laws regarding waste?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.B: Standard Organization of Nigeria
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Federal Ministry of Environment

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment takes the lead in creating national policies and rules to protect the environment from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why is proper health care waste management strictly regulated in clinical settings?

options.A: To ensure the facility uses less electricity every month
options.B: To make hospital compounds look neat for visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent the spread of infections and protect community health
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing office supplies

explanation: Strict rules are necessary because improperly managed medical waste can transmit dangerous diseases to staff, patients, and the public. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is classified as pathological waste?

options.A: Used office paper and empty cardboard boxes
options.B: Expired paracetamol syrup bottles
options.C: Recognizable human tissues and body parts
options.D: Disposable plastic food plates

explanation: Pathological waste specifically refers to body parts, tissues, and organs removed during surgeries or autopsies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: A nurse discards an empty glass drug ampoule. Which waste category does this item belong to?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Sharps
options.C: Paper waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Even though ampoules are glass rather than needles, their sharp edges can easily cut skin, so they must be treated as sharps waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

options.A: After the cleaning staff transport it outside
options.B: At the exact point and time of generation
options.C: Only when the waste bins are completely full
options.D: During the final incineration process

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately where the waste is produced to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of filling a waste collection bag to the absolute brim?

options.A: It violates local tax laws regarding commercial building capacity
options.B: It automatically changes the chemical composition of the waste inside
options.C: It increases the risk of spills, tears, and accidental injuries during handling
options.D: It makes the waste lighter and harder for handlers to grip

explanation: Overfilled bags are difficult to tie securely and prone to bursting or puncturing, exposing staff to injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which feature is essential for a central health care waste storage room?

options.A: Carpeted flooring for noise reduction
options.B: Large glass windows for direct sunlight exposure
options.C: Open access for patients and visitors
options.D: Secure locks to prevent unauthorized entry

explanation: Central storage areas must be locked securely to keep unauthorized persons, scavengers, and animals away from hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why must internal transport routes avoid patient dining areas and crowded waiting rooms?

options.A: To minimize the risk of accidental exposure and public anxiety
options.B: To prevent the waste from cooling down too quickly
options.C: To ensure the waste carts move at a faster speed
options.D: To comply with architectural design rules for elevators

explanation: Moving hazardous waste through clean, crowded public spaces creates unnecessary infection risks and alarms patients. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is the primary mechanism of an autoclave in waste treatment?

options.A: Dissolving metal instruments in strong acids
options.B: Burning waste at extremely high open flames
options.C: Freezing biological specimens to sub-zero temperatures
options.D: Steam sterilization under high pressure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to kill all infectious agents present in medical waste effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is encapsulation often used specifically for pharmaceutical waste?

options.A: To turn expired tablets into sweet-tasting liquid syrups
options.B: To immobilize chemical drugs and prevent them from entering water supplies
options.C: To bleach colored medicine bottles so they can be recycled
options.D: To make heavy metal containers easier to burn in an incinerator

explanation: Encapsulation binds drugs in a solid matrix like cement, stopping them from dissolving and leaching into soil and groundwater. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the tiny puncture wound tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow joint

explanation: Immediate washing helps remove and flush out infectious pathogens before they can establish an infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: What does the concept of universal precautions mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Using disposable plastic syringes only once per hospital
options.B: Testing every single admitted patient for rare tropical diseases
options.C: Treating all blood and body fluids as if they are infectious
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every routine physical exam

explanation: Universal precautions assume every patient's fluids carry blood-borne pathogens, ensuring staff use protection consistently. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: A nurse walks into a ward and finds a junior colleague throwing a used syringe into a regular black polythene bag. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Correct the colleague immediately and ensure the syringe is moved to the sharps box
options.B: Ignore the mistake because cleaners will sort it out later anyway
options.C: Write an official query letter to the hospital medical director
options.D: Remove all waste bins from the ward to teach everyone a lesson

explanation: Nurses have a duty to correct segregation errors instantly to maintain a safe working and clinical environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why is nurse-led education for patients and visitors important for waste management?

options.A: To train family members how to incinerate trash in the hospital yard
options.B: To encourage visitors to bring their own waste bags from home
options.C: To prevent visitors from accidentally touching hazardous waste or opening bins
options.D: To reduce the hospital budget spent on buying cleaning detergents

explanation: Visitors often do not know clinical waste risks, so nursing guidance keeps them from touching contaminated materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why is health care waste management so important in our hospitals?

options.A: To increase the speed of patient discharge procedures
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of running a hospital
options.C: To eliminate the need for cleaning hospital floors
options.D: To protect public health and the environment from harm

explanation: You got this! Proper waste management stops dangerous materials from spreading infections or polluting our communities. Great job thinking about safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: As a bedside nurse, why are you considered right at the center of hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses are the only staff members allowed to touch trash
options.B: Nurses are legally liable for the city waste trucks
options.C: Nurses generate waste during daily patient care activities
options.D: Hospital management forces nurses to pay for disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because we give direct patient care every day, we are the first ones to handle and discard medical materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: Under which waste category do used injection needles and blades fall?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pathological waste
options.C: Sharps
options.D: General waste

explanation: Correct! Needles and piercing instruments are always called 'sharps' because of the puncture risk they carry. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: How is general hospital waste different from infectious waste?

options.A: Infectious waste is always heavier than general waste boxes
options.B: General waste requires special incineration before leaving the ward
options.C: General waste is non-hazardous and similar to normal household trash
options.D: Infectious waste comes only from the hospital kitchen

explanation: Exactly! General waste has no contamination risk (like empty paper packaging), unlike infectious items that carry pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which government bodies usually set the rules for healthcare waste management?

options.A: Ministries of health and environmental agencies
options.B: Patient advocacy groups and volunteer clubs
options.C: Local taxi drivers unions and market associations
options.D: Private pharmaceutical manufacturing companies

explanation: Well done! Government health and environmental sectors hold the legal duty to set safety standards for everyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the main goal of laws and policies guiding waste disposal in healthcare?

options.A: To generate revenue through heavy facility fines
options.B: To make hospital paperwork as complicated as possible
options.C: To restrict the purchase of medical equipment
options.D: To standardize safe practices and protect public safety

explanation: You got it! Laws ensure every clinic and hospital follows clear, uniform rules to keep staff and patients safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: At what point should waste sorting (segregation) happen in the clinical ward?

options.A: At the end of the nursing shift
options.B: When the cleaner arrives with large trucks
options.C: After the waste reaches the municipal dump
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right where you use it prevents dangerous mix-ups and keeps everyone handling it safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: You notice the safety box on your treatment trolley is about three-quarters full. What should you do?

options.A: Seal the container and replace it with a new one
options.B: Push the contents down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.C: Transfer some needles into a regular black plastic bag
options.D: Leave it open until the end of the week to save money

explanation: Safety first! Never push down or overfill sharp containers. Seal them at three-quarters full to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in treating medical waste?

options.A: Freezing body tissues for long-term storage
options.B: Crushing glass bottles into fine reusable sand
options.C: Sterilizing infectious items using high-pressure steam
options.D: Dissolving expired pharmaceutical tablets in acid

explanation: Correct! Autoclaves use high heat and steam to kill off pathogens before the waste leaves the facility. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why must internal waste transport trolleys always be covered when moving through the hospital?

options.A: To make the trolleys move faster down the ramp
options.B: To keep the trash bags cool under direct sunlight
options.C: To hide unpleasant sights from the hospital visitors
options.D: To prevent accidental spills and exposure along hospital corridors

explanation: You nailed it! Covering the trolley stops items from falling out and protects patients and staff walking in the hallways. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which infection is a nurse most afraid of contracting after an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: That's right! Blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV are our biggest concerns after a sharp injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after sustaining a needle stick injury while on duty?

options.A: Hide the incident from the supervisor to avoid paperwork
options.B: Report the incident immediately for evaluation and prophylaxis
options.C: Soak the injured finger in cold river water
options.D: Take a strong painkiller and finish the remaining shift

explanation: Always report immediately! Quick action allows the occupational health team to give you prompt counseling and protective meds. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: How can clinical nurses positively influence waste management practices on their wards?

options.A: By writing national environmental laws in parliament
options.B: By driving the municipal garbage trucks on weekends
options.C: By buying new incineration machines for the hospital
options.D: By acting as role models and teaching junior staff correct sorting

explanation: Spot on! Your daily good habits teach junior colleagues and students how to do things the right way. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard duty for a clinical nurse regarding waste management?

options.A: Educating patients on safe disposal of personal medical items
options.B: Designing and building new municipal waste landfills
options.C: Reporting damaged or overfilled sharp containers
options.D: Segregating items into appropriate colored bins

explanation: Correct! Building landfills is the job of civil and environmental engineers, not clinical nurses. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: In a busy hospital, what percentage of the total waste produced is actually regular, non-hazardous household waste?

options.A: About 50%
options.B: About 99%
options.C: About 15%
options.D: About 85%

explanation: Most of what hospitals throw away is everyday rubbish (like paper and food packaging) that doesn't carry any infection risks. Only a small fraction is dangerous clinical waste! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which of these items counts as pathological waste?

options.A: Surgical gauze soaked in blood
options.B: An empty plastic intravenous fluid bag
options.C: A surgically removed human gallbladder
options.D: A used hypodermic needle and syringe

explanation: Pathological waste refers to body parts, tissues, or organs removed during surgery or autopsies. Neat to know for clinical sorting! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: What is the biggest danger to waste handlers when sharps accidentally get mixed into ordinary trash bags?

options.A: Contracting waterborne cholera
options.B: Suffering from acute chemical burns
options.C: Sustaining accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: Developing chronic asthma from dust

explanation: Loose needles can easily poke through regular bags and skin, putting anyone handling the trash at risk of injury and infection. Always watch your sharps! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: How can pouring leftover drugs down open drains harm our environment?

options.A: It triggers severe volcanic activity near water bodies
options.B: It contributes to antimicrobial resistance and harms aquatic life
options.C: It instantly freezes local rivers and kills vegetation
options.D: It causes immediate radioactive contamination in the soil

explanation: Drugs in our waterways expose local water animals and bacteria to medications, helping drug-resistant superbugs grow faster. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h2)

question: Which global health body leads the way in setting standards for medical waste management?

options.A: International Monetary Fund
options.B: World Health Organization
options.C: International Labour Organization
options.D: World Trade Organization

explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides the main guidelines and handbooks that countries follow to keep medical waste disposal safe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: Why do international health authorities want every country to have clear national policies on medical waste?

options.A: To ensure uniform taxation of hospital supplies
options.B: To establish legal accountability and standardize safe handling practices
options.C: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: To replace local hospital management boards with global inspectors

explanation: National rules give hospitals the legal backing and clear steps they need to handle dangerous materials safely every single day. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h3)

question: At what point in your clinical workflow should healthcare waste be sorted?

options.A: At the final incineration site
options.B: During the weekly municipal garbage collection
options.C: After transport to the central landfill
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops dangerous items from getting mixed up with regular trash. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: You just gave an injection on a busy ward. What is your very next step with that used needle?

options.A: Recap the needle carefully and place it in the regular paper bin
options.B: Throw the syringe into the general black bin bag
options.C: Leave the syringe on the bedside table for the cleaning staff
options.D: Drop the uncovered needle directly into a rigid safety box

explanation: Never recap needles! Drop them straight into a puncture-proof safety box to protect yourself and others from accidental pokes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: What main technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

options.A: Open-air burning
options.B: High-pressure steam sterilization
options.C: Deep underground freezing
options.D: Chemical dissolution in acid

explanation: Autoclaves use intense steam pressure to hit temperatures that wipe out germs and pathogens on medical items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why is incineration the go-to method for body parts and human tissues?

options.A: It completely destroys anatomical parts safely and respectfully through high heat
options.B: It turns biological tissues into safe fertilizer for crops
options.C: It allows tissues to be recycled into new plastic products
options.D: It is the cheapest way to produce electricity

explanation: High-heat incineration is a safe, hygienic way to dispose of anatomical waste while treating human remains with proper dignity. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered the heartbeat of safe hospital waste management?

options.A: They design and build medical incinerators
options.B: They purchase all hospital waste disposal bags
options.C: They generate and supervise the sorting of the majority of clinical waste
options.D: They write national environmental protection laws

explanation: Because nurses carry out most bedside procedures, your daily choices make or break how well hospital waste gets sorted! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is an important way nurses can guide patients and visitors regarding ward waste?

options.A: Revising the hospital's annual financial budget
options.B: Teaching them how to operate surgical autoclaves
options.C: Explaining the correct use of color-coded waste bins
options.D: Training them to administer intravenous injections

explanation: Visitors often toss things into the nearest bin. Taking a second to guide them helps keep our color-coded waste streams pure! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h6)

question: What is a major challenge for proper waste management in clinics with limited resources?

options.A: Strict enforcement of international laws
options.B: Excessive funding and overstaffing
options.C: Shortages of proper segregation supplies and erratic electricity
options.D: Too many advanced incinerators

explanation: Lack of steady power and basic items like safety boxes can make sticking to textbook waste rules tough in everyday rural practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: If your rural clinic runs out of official safety boxes, what is a safe, clever backup plan for used needles?

options.A: Using locally available, puncture-resistant rigid containers
options.B: Throwing loose needles directly into the regular dustbin
options.C: Burying uncapped needles in the hospital garden
options.D: Washing and reusing disposable needles for multiple patients

explanation: Improvise safely! Using a sturdy, thick local container keeps everyone safe from needle pricks until official disposal arrives. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the Basel Convention?

options.A: To control the movement and safe disposal of hazardous wastes across borders
options.B: To regulate the global trade of pharmaceutical medications
options.C: To set limits on greenhouse gas emissions from factories
options.D: To manage the disposal of standard household garbage in landfills

explanation: You've got this! The Basel Convention was set up specifically to stop the harmful practice of shipping dangerous industrial waste across international borders where it could harm communities. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: Why was the Basel Convention created back in the late 1980s?

options.A: Global hospitals were running out of space for medical syringes
options.B: Oceans were overflowing with plastic beverage containers
options.C: Air pollution from factories caused a sudden rise in global temperatures
options.D: Industrialized nations were dumping toxic waste in developing countries

explanation: Spot on! Wealthy countries used to ship their toxic industrial byproducts to poorer nations to save money. Public outrage over this unfair practice led directly to the treaty. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: Before the treaty, why did companies love to ship toxic waste to other countries?

options.A: Shipping companies received government tax breaks for exports
options.B: Developing nations had weak laws and lower disposal costs
options.C: Poorer countries urgently needed industrial ash for road building
options.D: Developing nations specifically requested toxic chemicals for farming

explanation: Exactly! Safe waste disposal is expensive. Companies saved money by taking advantage of countries that didn't yet have strict environmental laws. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: What happened when major scandals broke out about ships dumping toxic waste?

options.A: They forced world leaders to create a binding international waste treaty
options.B: They led to a complete ban on all maritime shipping worldwide
options.C: They encouraged developing nations to build more local incinerators
options.D: They proved that ocean water naturally neutralizes heavy metal toxins

explanation: Well done! When media and the public saw wandering ships dumping dangerous cargo, world leaders realized they had to step in with strict international rules. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: What does the 'Proximity Principle' mean when dealing with hazardous waste?

options.A: It should be shipped overseas to countries with large open spaces
options.B: It must be stored as far away from human populations as possible
options.C: It must be kept in temporary storage for at least ten years
options.D: It should be disposed of as close to its source as possible

explanation: You got it! Keeping travel distances short means fewer chances for accidental spills or exposure while moving dangerous materials around. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: Why does the Basel Convention emphasize stopping waste creation right at the source?

options.A: International shipping companies refuse to carry heavy metal byproducts
options.B: Preventing waste creation is safer than trying to manage it later
options.C: Governments want to completely shut down the chemical manufacturing sector
options.D: It is cheaper to burn hazardous waste in city centers than transport it

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If you don't create the toxic byproduct in the first place, you completely avoid the risks of transporting and disposing of it. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

options.A: Biodegradable
options.B: Odorless
options.C: Flammable
options.D: Transparent

explanation: That's right! Materials that are flammable, corrosive, toxic, or reactive are flagged as hazardous and heavily regulated. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: How do authorities decide if a substance is legally classified as hazardous waste?

options.A: By measuring how heavy the shipping container is when loaded onto a truck
options.B: By testing whether the material dissolves easily in clean drinking water
options.C: By checking if the manufacturing company is publicly traded on the stock market
options.D: By looking at its specific waste stream source or dangerous characteristics

explanation: Spot on! The treaty looks at where the waste came from and how it behaves (like if it's toxic or flammable) to classify it properly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: What does 'Prior Informed Consent (PIC)' require before hazardous waste can be exported?

options.A: Approval from international shipping insurance companies
options.B: A public vote in the exporting nation's capital city
options.C: Written approval from the importing and transit countries
options.D: Permission from the World Health Organization director

explanation: You're doing great! PIC means any country receiving the waste—plus any countries the cargo passes through—must give their official written permission first. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: If a company tries to ship chemical waste abroad without telling the countries it passes through, what happens under the Basel Convention?

options.A: The company receives a warning but the shipment continues
options.B: The transit nations must accept the cargo if fees are paid
options.C: The shipment is illegal and prohibited from moving
options.D: The waste is automatically classified as non-hazardous

explanation: Exactly! Skipping the paperwork and failing to notify every country involved makes the shipment completely illegal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which health issue is closely linked to heavy metal exposure from bad toxic waste disposal?

options.A: Neurological damage
options.B: Seasonal allergies
options.C: Vision improvement
options.D: Muscle hypertrophy

explanation: That's correct! Toxic metals like lead and mercury attack the nervous system, leading to serious brain and developmental issues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)

question: Why do low-resource communities usually suffer the most from improper toxic waste dumping?

options.A: Warm climates cause toxic waste to evaporate completely into the upper atmosphere
options.B: They lack the robust infrastructure needed to detect and treat contamination
options.C: Local hospitals specialize in reversing the effects of heavy metal poisoning
options.D: Their residents willingly consume industrial chemicals for traditional remedies

explanation: You nailed it. Communities with fewer resources often struggle to test their water or provide medical care for long-term toxic exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)

question: You see a colleague pouring leftover liquid antibiotics down the hospital sink. What is the right nursing response?

options.A: Help pour the remaining bottles down the drain to finish faster
options.B: Stop the colleague and explain proper pharmaceutical waste disposal
options.C: Throw the empty glass bottles into the general household trash bin
options.D: Ignore the action since liquid drugs dissolve safely in water pipes

explanation: Fantastic clinical judgment! Pouring medications down regular drains pollutes local water systems. Proper disposal protects both our patients and our environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of stock holding conventions in a nursing unit?

options.A: Reducing the salary budget of nursing staff
options.B: Increasing the number of beds in the ward
options.C: Ensuring vital supplies are available when needed
options.D: Complying with hospital architectural designs

explanation: Stock holding conventions focus mainly on making sure medical items and drugs are always ready for patient care without shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Why must nurses understand basic inventory and stock control principles?

options.A: To design new storage shelves for the hospital
options.B: To negotiate better prices with medical suppliers
options.C: To take over the job of the hospital pharmacist
options.D: To prevent emergency supply shortages on the ward

explanation: Nurses handle ward supplies every day, so knowing stock rules helps them prevent running out of critical items during patient care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a consumable medical supply?

options.A: An overhead patient bed
options.B: A mercury sphygmomanometer
options.C: A hospital wheelchair
options.D: Disposable syringes

explanation: Consumables are single-use items that get thrown away after one application, like syringes and gauze. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: How should emergency stock items on a ward be managed differently from regular supplies?

options.A: Ordered only once a year to cut down on paperwork
options.B: Checked daily and replaced immediately after any use
options.C: Stored in a locked room away from all nursing staff
options.D: Kept in open corridors for easy public access

explanation: Emergency items must be ready at a moment's notice, requiring daily checks and instant replenishment if used. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: What does the FIFO stock rotation rule stand for?

options.A: Free-Issue, Fixed-Order
options.B: Final-Inspection, First-Order
options.C: First-In, First-Out
options.D: Fast-Item, Fast-Out

explanation: FIFO means the items that arrived first on the shelf should be the ones picked and used first. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: A nurse receives a fresh batch of IV antibiotics. Where should the nurse place them relative to the older stock already on the shelf?

options.A: Inside the nurse's personal locker
options.B: Behind the older stock
options.C: On a completely different floor
options.D: In front of the older stock

explanation: Placing new stock behind older stock ensures the older items are picked first, practicing FIFO and preventing expiration. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h3)

question: What does the reorder point represent in inventory management?

options.A: The cost of buying a single medical item
options.B: The date when a medication finally expires
options.C: The maximum number of items a shelf can hold
options.D: The specific stock level that triggers a new order

explanation: The reorder point is the threshold that tells the nurse or storekeeper it is time to buy more supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What happens if a nursing unit allows its stock levels to fall below the minimum safety threshold?

options.A: The storage room becomes much cleaner and easier to clean
options.B: The hospital pharmacy saves a lot of money on bulk purchases
options.C: Expired items automatically get removed from the shelves
options.D: Patients may face dangerous delays in treatment due to shortages

explanation: Falling below minimum safety stock means the ward risks running out of crucial supplies during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What should a nurse do if a sterile instrument pack has a torn or damp wrapper?

options.A: Discard or return the item because sterility is lost
options.B: Wipe the outside with alcohol and place it back on the shelf
options.C: Use it quickly before any dust can settle inside
options.D: Ask another nurse to approve using it for a minor dressing

explanation: Any damage or moisture to a sterile wrapper compromises the barrier, meaning the instruments are no longer safe to use. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

options.A: To ensure the refrigerator door is locked at all times
options.B: To check if the electricity bill is too high for the ward
options.C: To make sure improper heat does not ruin drug potency
options.D: To calculate how many patients received injections that day

explanation: Many pharmaceutical products degrade quickly if temperatures fluctuate outside the safe cold chain range. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of failing to record items taken from the ward inventory?

options.A: The medications on the shelf will expire much faster than normal
options.B: The hospital will automatically order double the amount needed
options.C: Patients will recover faster because fewer drugs are logged
options.D: Stock counts will not match actual inventory, causing unexpected shortages

explanation: Unrecorded items create hidden inventory gaps, making reorder calculations inaccurate and leading to sudden stockouts. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: What is the correct action when a nurse discovers a box of expired intravenous fluids in the treatment room?

options.A: Donate it to a local clinic outside the hospital system
options.B: Use it quickly for non-critical patients before anyone notices
options.C: Hide it at the back of the cupboard until the next audit
options.D: Remove it from the shelf and follow proper waste disposal protocols

explanation: Expired items must be isolated and disposed of safely to ensure they are never accidentally given to a patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to keep expired medication anywhere near active stock supplies?

options.A: It creates a high risk of accidentally administering degraded drugs to a patient
options.B: It automatically invalidates the expiry dates of neighboring boxes
options.C: It takes up space that should be used for cleaning supplies
options.D: It causes the electric lights in the storage room to flicker

explanation: Closeness to active stock increases the chance that a busy nurse will grab an expired item during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.B: To speed up medication administration during busy ward shifts
options.C: To ensure patients experience zero pain during every procedure
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

explanation: Injection safety encompasses protective measures for everyone involved in or affected by the injection process, preventing infections and injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is an injection considered a high-risk procedure despite its daily frequency?

options.A: It requires specialized surgical equipment to perform safely
options.B: It bypasses the body's natural skin barrier and enters sterile tissues directly
options.C: It is the only medical procedure that causes severe allergic reactions
options.D: It is always performed in emergency situations without preparation

explanation: Because a needle breaks the skin, any contamination on the equipment or technique introduces pathogens straight into the body, bypassing primary defenses. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: What happens if you use a single-dose medication vial for more than one patient?

options.A: It changes the chemical concentration of the prescribed drug
options.B: It transfers invisible pathogens between patients via contaminated equipment
options.C: It causes the remaining medicine to expire instantly
options.D: It increases the physical pain experienced during injection

explanation: Single-dose vials don't have preservatives. Reusing them lets germs multiply and spread infections to the next patient. Always use one vial per patient! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why should you never use both hands to recap a used needle?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes the injection painful
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.C: It violates hospital policies regarding medication waste disposal
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy medication round

explanation: Using two hands to recap makes it way too easy to miss the cap and puncture your own finger. Safety first—keep that hand away from the sharp end! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which virus is notorious for surviving on medical equipment and surfaces for days, making it very easy to spread if equipment is reused?

options.A: Influenza Virus
options.B: Streptococcus Pneumoniae
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Hepatitis B Virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is a tough survivor and can live on surfaces and tools outside the body for days. That's why strict sterilization and single-use rules are non-negotiable. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: A nurse changes a contaminated needle but reuses the plastic syringe barrel for another patient. What is the big danger here?

options.A: It causes an immediate allergic reaction in the patient
options.B: It transfers blood-borne pathogens trapped inside the barrel
options.C: It causes severe muscle necrosis at the injection site
options.D: It neutralizes the therapeutic effect of the injected drug

explanation: Remember, fluids and tiny amounts of blood pull back into the barrel during use. Changing just the needle isn't enough; the whole syringe must be single-use! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is a major complication if an intramuscular injection is given incorrectly in the buttocks?

options.A: Sudden elevation of intraocular pressure
options.B: Sciatic nerve injury leading to pain or paralysis
options.C: Immediate development of systemic respiratory failure
options.D: Complete blockage of the carotid artery

explanation: The sciatic nerve runs right through the lower, inner part of the buttock. This is why proper site landmarks (like the upper outer quadrant) are so crucial! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do unsterile injection techniques lead to painful abscesses?

options.A: By introducing bacteria from the skin surface deep into the muscle tissue
options.B: By causing an immediate chemical reaction that dissolves bone tissue
options.C: By increasing the local blood flow until the tissue swells and bursts
options.D: By freezing the surrounding muscle fibers and destroying blood vessels

explanation: When germs are pushed past the skin into warm muscle, they multiply, cause inflammation, and form pus (an abscess). Good antisepsis stops this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h4)

question: What causes most needle-stick injuries among nursing students and staff?

options.A: Attempting to recap used needles
options.B: Administering intravenous medications too quickly
options.C: Reading patient charts near the bedside
options.D: Washing contaminated glass ampoules

explanation: Recapping used needles is a leading cause of accidental pricks because a slip of the hand means a direct puncture. Never recap if you can avoid it! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are overfilled sharps containers dangerous on the ward?

options.A: They attract insects and rodents into patient care areas
options.B: They release toxic chemical fumes into the nursing station
options.C: They expose workers to protruding needles and unstable sharp items
options.D: They prevent the automated counting of used syringes

explanation: Once a sharps box is past its fill line, needles start stacking up near the top and can easily prick the next person trying to dispose of waste. Close them on time! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the single best way to stop infections from spreading in any healthcare setting?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns for every procedure
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Using disposable plastic trays

explanation: Simple handwashing or alcohol rubbing is your superpower against hospital infections. It removes germs picked up from patients and surroundings instantly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: How should you clean a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Wiping in a circular motion from the center outward and letting it dry
options.B: Applying an antiseptic spray and immediately inserting the needle
options.C: Wiping from the outer edges inward toward the center of the site
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth with a dry cotton ball

explanation: Always move from clean (center) to less clean (outward) to push germs away. Plus, letting the alcohol dry is what actually kills the microbes! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: If the hospital runs out of single-use syringes, what is the right way for a nurse to handle the situation?

options.A: By asking patients to purchase and bring their own needles from home
options.B: By skipping injections until the patient's condition improves naturally
options.C: By rinsing old syringes with hot water and reusing them for stable patients
options.D: By reporting the shortage and demanding proper supplies before performing injections

explanation: As a patient advocate, you must speak up and never compromise safety by taking shortcuts like equipment reuse. Patient safety comes first! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)

question: When caring for patients managing injections at home, what is a key duty for the nurse?

options.A: Disposing of patient sharps in regular household garbage bags
options.B: Instructing relatives to reuse syringes if they look clean
options.C: Teaching patients and families safe administration and disposal methods
options.D: Leaving used needles uncapped on the kitchen table for easy access

explanation: Great job! Educating patients and their families prevents accidental needle pricks in homes and communities after they leave the hospital. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of United Nations packaging requirements in healthcare?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of shipping medical laboratory supplies
options.B: To speed up the delivery time of routine blood test results
options.C: To ensure all medical specimens look identical to couriers
options.D: To prevent leaks and spills of hazardous materials during transit

explanation: These international rules are designed specifically to contain dangerous biological or chemical contents safely even if the outer box is dropped or crushed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: Who is primarily protected by the proper use of UN-certified transport packaging?

options.A: Hospital administrators managing the facility budget
options.B: Healthcare workers, couriers, and the general public
options.C: Patient family members waiting in the clinic lobby
options.D: Only the laboratory technicians performing the final analysis

explanation: Dangerous goods transit involves many handlers outside the hospital walls, making spill prevention vital for community health and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: Which UN number is typically used for routine diagnostic specimens classified as Category B biological substances?
explanation: Think of UN 3373 as the standard code you see on diamond labels for everyday lab samples like blood tubes. Easy to remember once you spot it a few times! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: What makes an infectious substance fit into Category A instead of Category B?

options.A: It can cause fatal or life-threatening disease upon exposure
options.B: It is shipped in much larger liquid volumes than normal samples
options.C: It only affects animals and never poses any risk to human health
options.D: It consists solely of routine urine and stool sample containers

explanation: Category A is for the scary, high-risk stuff that can cause severe or fatal illness, so it needs extra-tough packaging. Excellent practice for clinical safety! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h2)

question: In a UN packaging code, what does the letter 'G' tell you about the container?

options.A: It is a glass vial container
options.B: It is a fiberboard box
options.C: It is a plastic specimen bag
options.D: It is a steel liquid drum

explanation: The number 4 tells us it's a box, and G stands for fiberboard (cardboard). Simple code breaking! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h3)

question: Why do UN containers have packing group letters like X, Y, and Z stamped on them?

options.A: To show the degree of hazard and container strength required
options.B: To indicate the specific hospital ward the box originated from
options.C: To list the chemical manufacturer who produced the plastic box
options.D: To tell the courier the exact delivery room temperature needed

explanation: An 'X' rating means the package can handle high-risk items, while 'Y' and 'Z' are for moderate and lower risks. You are mastering the logistics! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h3)

question: Why do we place absorbent material inside the secondary packaging of a medical specimen?

options.A: To cushion the glass tubes against heavy outside vibration
options.B: To soak up all the liquid if the primary tube breaks
options.C: To keep the biological specimen frozen during long flights
options.D: To absorb moisture from the humid clinic room air

explanation: It's a built-in safety net! If a tube cracks, the absorbent material traps the fluid so it never leaks outside. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: How many layers make up the standard triple packaging system for infectious substances?

options.A: Three layers
options.B: One layer
options.C: Two layers
options.D: Four layers

explanation: The system consists of a primary receptacle, secondary packaging, and an outer packaging layer working together. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h4)

question: What do the double upward arrows on a medical shipping box mean?

options.A: The temperature range required inside the shipping compartment
options.B: The correct upright orientation to prevent liquid leaks
options.C: The maximum stacking limit allowed for storage in the warehouse
options.D: The direction the delivery vehicle must drive to reach the lab

explanation: Those arrows must point straight up so the liquid tubes inside stay upright and don't leak through their caps. Good clinical detail to know! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h5)

question: Why must a 24-hour emergency phone number be on hazardous material shipping documents?

options.A: To provide immediate expert guidance if a spill or exposure occurs
options.B: To let the receiving nurse ask about patient clinical history
options.C: To schedule the exact pickup time for the next laboratory batch
options.D: To allow the courier to confirm the payment receipt with accounting

explanation: If there's an accident on the road, emergency responders need someone to call instantly who knows how to handle that specific hazard safely. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h5)

question: A nurse is getting blood tubes ready to send to a lab across town. What should she do first?

options.A: Attach a 24-hour emergency contact phone number directly onto the patient's arm
options.B: Drop the loose glass tubes directly into a standard red plastic hospital waste bag
options.C: Verify that tube caps are tightly sealed and place them into an approved secondary container
options.D: Wrap the unsecured tubes in paper towels and place them in an ordinary cardboard shoe box

explanation: Safety first! Always check that caps are secure and use the proper secondary container before moving samples off-site. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h6)

question: As a nurse, which common transport mistake should you always avoid?

options.A: Checking patient identification labels against the laboratory request forms
options.B: Wearing clean gloves while handling outside surfaces of specimen tubes
options.C: Assuming standard hospital trash bags are sufficient for off-site transport
options.D: Wiping down secondary containers if a minor drop of fluid touches the outside

explanation: Regular waste bags are not strong enough or certified for road transport. Always use approved UN-certified packaging for safety! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in nursing practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing medical supplies
options.B: To ensure injections do no harm to the patient or worker
options.C: To speed up the administration of routine vaccinations
options.D: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting patients, healthcare workers, and the community from injury and disease transmission during injection procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why are unsafe injection practices such a big public health problem?

options.A: They make injectable medications completely ineffective
options.B: They increase the physical pain of receiving treatment
options.C: They rapidly spread blood-borne pathogens to large numbers of people
options.D: They cause immediate allergic reactions in all recipients

explanation: Sharing needles or contaminating medication vials can quickly transmit serious blood-borne infections across many patients in a short time. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which virus from unsafe injections can survive on surfaces outside the body for at least seven days?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Ebola virus
options.D: Hepatitis C virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is very tough and can remain infectious on environmental surfaces for a week or more. Always treat gear with care! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h2)

question: Besides blood-borne viruses, what other common infection can result from using non-sterile injection equipment?

options.A: Bacterial infections causing abscesses and sepsis
options.B: Fungal infections affecting the respiratory tract
options.C: Parasitic infections residing in the bloodstream
options.D: Genetic disorders altering red blood cells

explanation: Unsterile equipment introduces bacteria straight into tissues, which can lead to painful local abscesses or severe blood infections like sepsis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which blood-borne pathogen carries the highest risk of infection after just a single accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B has a very high concentration in the blood, making it the most easily transmitted pathogen following a needle-stick accident. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h3)

question: How do Hepatitis B and C viruses primarily cause damage inside the human body?

options.A: By blocking oxygen transport in red blood cells
options.B: By releasing toxins that paralyze skeletal muscles
options.C: By destroying CD4+ immune cells in the bloodstream
options.D: By targeting hepatocytes and triggering liver inflammation

explanation: Both Hepatitis B and C love to attack liver cells (hepatocytes), causing inflammation and gradual damage over time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute viral hepatitis develops jaundice (yellow skin and eyes)?

options.A: Excessive breakdown of red blood cells in the spleen
options.B: Blockage of the main pancreatic duct by scar tissue
options.C: Impaired bilirubin processing by the inflamed liver
options.D: Accumulation of white blood cells in skin tissues

explanation: When the liver is inflamed by hepatitis, it can't process bilirubin properly. It builds up in the body, giving the skin and eyes that yellow color. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h4)

question: A patient comes in with fever, right upper tummy pain, dark urine, and yellow eyes a few weeks after getting injections at an unlicensed clinic. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Acute viral hepatitis
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic kidney disease
options.D: Acute bacterial sepsis

explanation: Dark urine and yellow eyes (jaundice) are classic signs of liver trouble like acute viral hepatitis, often linked to unsafe injection exposures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h4)

question: What common belief often drives high injection rates among patients in many local communities?

options.A: The recommendation of international health organizations
options.B: The lower financial cost of receiving intravenous drugs
options.C: The absence of any side effects from injectable drugs
options.D: The belief that injections work faster than oral medications

explanation: Many people strongly prefer injections because of the common myth that drugs given by needle cure illnesses much faster than pills. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge that leads to unsafe injection practices in low-resource settings?

options.A: High patient demand for parenteral treatments
options.B: Shortages of single-use sterile injection equipment
options.C: An overabundance of certified auto-disable syringes
options.D: The operation of informal and unregulated drug vendors

explanation: Facilities actually suffer from shortages of safe equipment, not an overabundance! Lack of supplies is a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which nursing action is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries and must be avoided?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands
options.B: Wearing clean gloves during procedures
options.C: Using single-dose medication vials
options.D: Performing hand hygiene before patient contact

explanation: Recapping used needles is a dangerous habit that frequently leads to accidental finger pricks. Keep safety first and drop them straight into the bin! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why do we prefer single-dose medication vials over multi-dose vials in clinical practice?

options.A: They are always cheaper to purchase in bulk
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medication calculations
options.C: They reduce the risk of cross-contamination between patients
options.D: They can be stored indefinitely at room temperature

explanation: Multi-dose vials can easily pick up germs if needles touch them repeatedly. Single-dose vials keep things clean and safe for every patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h6)

question: At what point should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced to keep everyone safe?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Halfway full
options.C: Completely filled to the brim
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Never overfill a sharps bin! Closing it when it's three-quarters full ensures protruding needles won't accidentally prick anyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h7)

question: What are two essential features of a proper sharps disposal container?

options.A: It must be puncture-resistant and leak-proof
options.B: It must be washed and reused between patients
options.C: It must be made of soft, flexible cardboard
options.D: It must be transparent to monitor waste levels

explanation: Sharps containers must be tough enough to stop needles from poking through and solid enough to keep any fluids inside. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the recommended maximum time window to start HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) after a needle-stick injury?

options.A: 72 hours
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 1 week

explanation: Time matters! PEP for HIV should be started as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of the exposure, to be most effective. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h8)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do after accidentally getting pricked by a used needle?

options.A: Cover the puncture with a bandage without washing
options.B: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out old blood
options.C: Wash the wound immediately with soap and water
options.D: Scrub the puncture site vigorously with bleach

explanation: Wash the spot gently with soap and running water right away. Avoid squeezing or harsh scrubbing, as that can push germs deeper in. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h8)

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who insists on getting an injection instead of pills for a mild illness?

options.A: Explain that oral medications are often just as effective and much safer
options.B: Tell the patient that injections are illegal for treating mild illnesses
options.C: Refuse to speak with the patient until they accept the prescribed pills
options.D: Administer a harmless saline injection to satisfy their psychological need

explanation: Patient education works best when it's kind and respectful. Clear up the myth about injections while highlighting why safe oral meds are great. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h9)

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach program in a rural area with high rates of unsafe injections. What should be the main focus?

options.A: Encouraging residents to perform self-injections to avoid clinic queues
options.B: Educating residents on the risks of unsafe injections and the safety of oral alternatives
options.C: Distributing personal sharps containers for families to keep in their kitchens
options.D: Teaching community members how to safely sterilize glass syringes at home

explanation: Community outreach is all about building awareness! Teach people about injection risks and show them that safe oral medicines work wonders too. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h9)

question: What is the biggest risk of reusing disposable syringes in a clinic?

options.A: Transmission of blood-borne infections
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to leftover air
options.C: Permanent numbing of the injection site
options.D: Immediate breakdown of the plastic barrel
